name: PISHE PASHA
description: Pishe Pasha is a two-player competitive patience game played in Jewish communities in North America since at least the mid-twentieth century. Each player has a face-down stock of 26 cards. Players get rid of cards by building foundation piles (Ace through King in each suit) or by playing onto the opponent's discard pile (next higher or lower rank). The first to empty their stock and discard wins.

content.text: Pishe Pasha is a two-player competitive patience game played in Jewish communities in North America since at least the mid-twentieth century. Each player has a face-down stock of 26 cards. Players get rid of cards by building foundation piles (Ace through King in each suit) or by playing onto the opponent's discard pile (next higher or lower rank). The first to empty their stock and discard wins.

Played in America, primarily in Jewish communities, since at least the mid-twentieth century; presumably originated in Europe. Many slight variations and spellings exist (Pisha Pasha, Pisha Paysha, Persian Pasha).
Usually two players (three possible; see variations). No partnerships.

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
Cards shuffled; each player receives a stock of 26 cards face down. Traditionally the first cards are dealt two at a time, the remainder three at a time.

items.text: Stop rule: Some play without the stop rule: a player who fails to play to a foundation can be forced to correct the mistake, but the turn continues.

Compulsory play on opponent's pile: If at any point during your turn the card you draw or the top of your discard does not fit a foundation but does fit the opponent's discard, it must be played there. Calling 'Pishe Pasha' on opponent error ends their turn; you may transfer cards from your discard to theirs if they fit, and transfer the bottom three (or one/two in milder versions) of your stock to the bottom of theirs.

Three-player game: Each player has 17 cards; one face-up card starts a single center foundation built upward regardless of suit (continuing king to ace to two). Compulsory to play to center when possible; otherwise play next higher or lower on either opponent's discard, or discard to your own pile. Turn passes clockwise.

Simple book version (Pisha Pasha): A simpler game of pure chance, similar to War: players divide the pack, turn top cards simultaneously; same suit the higher card takes the opponent's discard pile. First to collect all cards wins. Often documented in books under Pisha Pasha.
